sanity_expectations: P is monotone non-decreasing in E (dP/dE >= 0 everywhere)
P bounded: |P| < Ps for finite E, and P -> Ps as E -> +infinity
Low-field linearity: P ≈ alpha*E when alpha*E << Ps (slope alpha at origin)
Odd symmetry P(-E) = -P(E) if extended to negative E
excitation_report: Single term Ps*tanh(alpha*E/Ps): rms 0.2165 over E∈[0, 2e8], sigma_multiple = 43.3 (>> 5). No weak terms; no parent so no new-term multiple. Auto_balance converged with no coefficient changes.
role_corrections: E: V->V (confirmed as sampled independent variable, applied field)
Ps: V->P (overridden: dielectric type is fixed, so Ps is a material saturation constant, not a sampled axis)
alpha: P->P (confirmed as fixed material parameter, low-field polarizability)
rationale: Static explicit relation P = Ps*tanh(alpha*E/Ps). Only E is an experimentally sampled axis; Ps and alpha are fixed material properties (the phenomenon states 'dielectric type is fixed'), so Ps is reclassified from input to parameter. Physical magnitudes: Ps=0.25 C/m^2 (BaTiO3-like ferroelectric), alpha=5e-9 F/m (ε0·χ for a moderately polarizable dielectric). E range [0, 2e8] V/m spans alpha*E/Ps in [0,4], covering both the linear (P≈alpha*E) and saturation (P→Ps) regimes so the tanh nonlinearity is fully expressed in the data. sigma=0.005 (~2% of Ps) is small vs the saturation amplitude yet catches the low-field slope. No parent generation, so no new-term check needed.
